findings.title: SMB exposed
findings.description: SMB file sharing has a long history of serious remote exploits (e.g. EternalBlue / WannaCry) and is a common ransomware entry point.
findings.recommendation: Block port 445 at the firewall except for trusted internal hosts; disable SMBv1 and keep the system patched.

findings.title: RDP exposed
findings.description: Remote Desktop is heavily targeted by password-guessing attacks and has had critical vulnerabilities (e.g. BlueKeep).
findings.recommendation: Do not expose RDP directly. Put it behind a VPN or gateway, enforce Network Level Authentication, strong passwords and MFA.

findings.title: Backdoored vsftpd version
findings.description: Detected vsftpd 2.3.4. vsftpd 2.3.4 was distributed with a known backdoor (CVE-2011-2523) that gives an attacker a root shell.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade vsftpd immediately and investigate the host for compromise.

findings.title: Very old OpenSSH
findings.description: Detected OpenSSH 4.7p1 Debian 8ubuntu1. OpenSSH versions before 7.0 are many years old and affected by multiple known vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Check the vendor's security advisories (distributions may backport fixes without changing the version number) and upgrade if affected.

findings.title: Telnet exposed
findings.description: Telnet sends usernames, passwords and all data in plain text, so anyone on the network path can read them.
findings.recommendation: Disable Telnet and use SSH instead.

findings.title: End-of-life Apache httpd
findings.description: Detected Apache httpd 2.2.8. Apache httpd versions before 2.4 are end-of-life and no longer receive security fixes.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to a supported Apache 2.4 release.

findings.title: SMB exposed
findings.description: SMB file sharing has a long history of serious remote exploits (e.g. EternalBlue / WannaCry) and is a common ransomware entry point.
findings.recommendation: Block port 445 at the firewall except for trusted internal hosts; disable SMBv1 and keep the system patched.

findings.title: FTP exposed
findings.description: FTP sends credentials and files in plain text and may allow anonymous login.
findings.recommendation: Replace with SFTP or FTPS, and disable anonymous access.

findings.title: NetBIOS session service exposed
findings.description: NetBIOS can leak information about the host, users and shares, and is an older way of reaching SMB.
findings.recommendation: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP if it is not needed, or firewall it.

findings.title: Database port exposed
findings.description: Database servers should rarely be reachable directly from other networks; exposure invites password guessing and exploits.
findings.recommendation: Firewall the database so only the application servers that need it can connect.

findings.title: Outdated MySQL
findings.description: Detected MySQL 5.0.51a-3ubuntu5. MySQL versions before 8.0 are end-of-life.
findings.recommendation: Upgrade to a supported MySQL release.

findings.title: Unencrypted HTTP
findings.description: The web service is served over plain HTTP, so traffic (including any logins) can be read or modified in transit.
findings.recommendation: Serve the site over HTTPS and redirect HTTP to HTTPS.
